raw_documents.text: USDA NASS reports corn harvest at 33% for the week ending 2026-10-11 across 18 selected states, versus 23% a week earlier and a 39% average for 2021-2025. Those states harvested 93% of the 2025 corn acreage. USDA NASS estimates soybean harvest at 46% across 18 selected states, compared with 25% a week earlier and a 50% average for 2021-2025. Those states harvested 96% of the 2025 soybean acreage. Adding the USDA NASS corn condition estimates of 44% good and 12% excellent gives 56%, versus a calculated 54% the previous week. This corn panel covers 18 states that planted 91% of the 2025 corn acreage. Adding the USDA NASS soybean condition estimates of 46% good and 11% excellent gives 57%, unchanged from the previous week. This soybean panel covers 18 states that planted 96% of the 2025 soybean acreage. Iowa corn harvest is 14%, compared with a 34% five-year average; Iowa soybean harvest is 31%, compared with 59%. Harvest completion and condition estimates do not measure yield, prices or company earnings. Publication was 2026-10-13 and observations ended 2026-10-11. Corresponding prior-year estimates are unavailable because reports were cancelled during the October-November 2025 federal funding lapse. All cited 2021-2025 averages combine published 2021-2024 and imputed 2025 estimates. NASS describes a non-probability survey of approximately 3,600 respondents making subjective observations. The estimates are acreage-weighted and subject to revision the following week; early responses may project weekend changes. Corn and soybeans use different 18-state panels. NASS weights harvest progress by average harvested acreage over the preceding three crop years, and condition by average planted acreage; the aggregates are not simple state averages.
